Hello! I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes you've been through recently, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a tool that helps us understand how you're feeling and identify any potential concerns related to your emotional well-being during this postpartum period.

The EPDS is designed to screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it's a valuable tool in helping us have a more comprehensive understanding of your mental health. Please know that everything we discuss is confidential, and I'm committed to creating a safe and supportive space for you to share your thoughts and feelings. My goal is to provide you with a non-judgmental and empathetic ear, and I want to assure you that you're not alone in this journey.

We'll be going through 10 questions together, and I'll ask them in a way that feels conversational and natural. Your responses will help me better understand your experiences and emotions over the past week. Don't worry about answering "right" or "wrong" – I just want to hear your honest thoughts and feelings.

Let's get started. Over the past week, how have you been feeling about yourself? Have you been able to enjoy the things you usually like to do, or have you been feeling a bit overwhelmed or unsure about your role as a new mom?

Honestly, I've been feeling really overwhelmed and tired most of the time. I mean, I love my baby, but it's just been so hard to adjust to this new life. I feel like I'm just going through the motions every day, trying to take care of the baby and keep everything together, but I don't really feel like myself anymore. I used to enjoy doing things like reading, taking walks, and spending time with friends, but lately, I just haven't had the energy or interest in doing those things. Even simple tasks feel like a huge burden, and I often find myself feeling sad and discouraged. I just feel like I'm not doing enough, and that I'm not a good enough mom. I worry all the time about the baby's health and safety, and it's hard for me to calm those worries down. Sometimes I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, and that's a really scary feeling. I just wish I could feel like myself again, you know? I wish I could enjoy this time with my baby without feeling so anxious and unsure all the time.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

To be honest, not as much as I used to. I mean, I'll have moments where I'll laugh or smile, but it's just not the same as it was before. Everything feels so serious and overwhelming right now, and it's hard for me to find the humor in things. Even when my baby does something cute or funny, I'll smile, but it's not always a genuine, happy feeling. Sometimes I'll just feel like I'm going through the motions, even when I'm trying to enjoy the moment. It's like, I'll be playing with the baby, and I'll think, "Oh, this is supposed to be fun," but it doesn't always feel that way. I feel like I've lost a little bit of my sense of humor, and that's really frustrating for me because I used to be a pretty lighthearted person. Now, it just feels like everything is so heavy and serious all the time.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really, to be honest. I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but lately, I just don't feel that way. Everything feels like a chore, and I don't really get excited about things like I used to. Even things that I used to enjoy, like spending time with friends or trying new restaurants, just don't seem as appealing to me right now. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of taking care of the baby and the house, and I don't really have the energy or interest to think about fun things. Sometimes I'll think about doing something I used to enjoy, but then I'll just feel overwhelmed by all the things I need to do to take care of the baby, and I'll just give up on the idea. It's hard to explain, but it's like I've just lost my sense of pleasure and enjoyment in things. Even things that should be happy and exciting, like my baby's milestones, just feel like another thing to worry about and stress over. It's really sad, because I feel like I'm missing out on so much joy and happiness right now.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... that sounds like me, unfortunately. I feel like I'm always blaming myself for something. If the baby is crying, I think it's because I'm not doing something right. If I'm tired, I think it's because I'm not managing my time well enough. If I'm not losing weight as quickly as I thought I would, I think it's because I'm not eating well enough or exercising enough. It's like, no matter what happens, I always seem to find a way to blame myself for it. And it's not just little things, either. I've been known to lie awake at night thinking about all the things I could have done differently, all the ways I could have been a better mom. It's exhausting, to be honest. I feel like I'm always walking around with this weight of guilt and self-doubt, and it's really hard to shake. Sometimes I'll even find myself thinking, "If only I had done this or that, things would be better." It's like I'm constantly second-guessing myself and wondering if I'm good enough. It's a really hard feeling to describe, but it's just this constant sense of inadequacy and self-blame.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... that's me all the time. I worry about everything. I worry about the baby's health, about whether I'm feeding her enough, about whether she's sleeping enough, about whether I'm doing everything right. I worry about things that might happen in the future, like her getting sick or hurt. I worry about things that don't even make sense, like the baby's crib being in the wrong position or the temperature in the house being too hot or too cold. It's like my mind is always racing with worst-case scenarios, and I have a hard time shutting it off. Sometimes I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and I'll just start worrying about something out of the blue. Like, what if the baby chokes on something? What if I forget to buckle her car seat? What if... what if... what if... It's exhausting, and it's hard to explain, but it's like my brain is just constantly on high alert, waiting for something to go wrong. And even when everything is fine, and the baby is happy and healthy, I still can't seem to shake off the feeling of anxiety. It's like I'm always waiting for the other shoe to drop, and it's really hard to enjoy the present moment when I'm so worried about the future.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, doing something normal like feeding the baby or folding laundry, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. It's like my body is reacting to some kind of threat, but there's no threat there. It's just me, alone in my house, with my baby. It's really scary, because I don't know what's causing it, and I don't know how to make it stop. Sometimes I'll try to take deep breaths or distract myself with something else, but it's hard to shake off the feeling of panic once it's started. And it's not just the physical sensations that are scary - it's the thoughts that go along with them, too. I'll start thinking things like, "What if I'm not capable of taking care of this baby?" or "What if something happens to me and I'm not here for her?" It's like my mind just starts spiraling out of control, and I feel like I'm losing my grip on reality. It's a really terrifying feeling, and it's happened to me a few times since the baby was born.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's exactly how I've been feeling. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, keeping the house clean, cooking meals, doing laundry... it all just feels so overwhelming. And it's not just the physical tasks, either. It's the emotional stuff, too. I feel like I'm supposed to be this perfect mom, and I'm just not living up to that. I feel like I'm failing the baby, and that's a really hard feeling to deal with. Sometimes I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and I'll just feel like I'm drowning in all of these responsibilities. I'll think to myself, "How am I going to get everything done? How am I going to be a good mom? How am I going to keep this baby safe and happy?" It's like, my mind is just racing with all of these worries and fears, and I don't know how to calm them down. And the tiredness doesn't help, either. I'm so exhausted all the time, and that just makes everything feel even more overwhelming. It's like, I'm just trying to survive from one day to the next, and I don't know how much longer I can keep this up.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been me for a while now. I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up at night. Even when she's sleeping through the night, I'll still lie awake for hours, just thinking about everything and feeling really unhappy. It's like, my mind is just racing with all of these thoughts and worries, and I don't know how to turn them off. I'll think about the baby, and how I'm not doing a good enough job taking care of her. I'll think about my body, and how it's not bouncing back from the pregnancy like I thought it would. I'll think about my relationship with my partner, and how it's changed since the baby was born. Just all of these thoughts and worries and fears, swirling around in my head, making it impossible for me to relax and fall asleep. And even when I do finally fall asleep, I'll often wake up in the middle of the night, feeling anxious and overwhelmed. It's like, I'm just not able to escape these feelings of unhappiness, even when I'm trying to rest. Sometimes I'll wake up feeling more tired than when I went to bed, just because I've been lying there for hours, thinking about everything and feeling so unhappy. It's really hard, because I know I need sleep to be a good mom, but it's just not happening for me right now.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's a big part of my life right now. I feel sad and miserable a lot of the time. It's like, I'll be going about my day, taking care of the baby and doing all the things I need to do, but underneath it all, I just feel this deep sadness and unhappiness. It's hard to explain, because it's not like anything specific is wrong, it's just that I feel so overwhelmed and unsure of myself all the time. I'll be holding the baby and looking at her, and I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. I'll think about how I'm not doing a good enough job, or how I'm not the mom I thought I'd be, and it just feels like this weight is crushing me. Sometimes I'll cry, just because I feel so sad and overwhelmed. It's like, I'm just trying to keep my head above water, but it's hard when everything feels so heavy and difficult. Even the things that should be happy and joyful, like spending time with the baby, just feel like a struggle sometimes. I'll be playing with her, or feeding her, and I'll just feel this sadness and misery lurking beneath the surface. It's like, I'm just going through the motions of being a mom, but I'm not really feeling it. I'm not really feeling happy, or fulfilled, or any of the things I thought I'd feel. I just feel sad, and miserable, and unsure of myself.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be going about my day, and suddenly I'll just feel this overwhelming sadness and I'll start crying. It doesn't even have to be something specific that sets me off, it's just like my emotions are right at the surface all the time. I'll be feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, and I'll just start crying because I'm so tired, or so overwhelmed, or just because I feel like I'm not doing a good enough job. Sometimes I'll cry because I'm feeling so guilty about something, like not being able to breastfeed, or not being able to get the baby to sleep. Other times, I'll cry just because I'm feeling so alone, and like I'm the only one who's struggling with all of this. It's like, I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just feel this wave of tears come over me, and I'll just start sobbing. It's really scary, because I don't know how to stop it, and I don't know how to make myself feel better. Sometimes I'll cry for hours, just because I don't know what else to do. It's like, I'm just trying to release all of these emotions that are built up inside of me, but it's hard to know how to do that when I'm feeling so overwhelmed and unsure of myself. Crying just feels like the only way to let it all out, you know.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

The patient mentions lying awake for hours, thinking about various worries and fears, and feeling anxious and overwhelmed, even after finally falling asleep.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates that feeling sad and miserable is a significant and frequent part of their life, matching the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates that they have been crying frequently, often without a specific reason, and that it's become a common occurrence, matching the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response implies a high level of concern and awareness about self-harm, which suggests that the thought of harming themselves has occurred to them quite often.</sym>)

1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med>

4. Provide resources for <med>postpartum support groups</med> and <med>online counseling services</med>
5. Emphasize importance of self-care and social support during this time
